title: x402 settlement counts get an authenticity-filtered public metric by Q2 2027
body: x402 settles AI-agent purchases as on-chain stablecoin transactions, which makes it unusual among agentic-commerce systems: its headline adoption number is a public ledger entry rather than a vendor claim, so an outsider can check it. A July 14 arXiv preprint by Shengchen Ling, Yajin Zhou, Lei Wu, and Cong Wang did check it, across 280 days of Base chain activity, and the number does not survive the audit. Of 136.7 million settlements moving $44.1 million, 21.20% are fictitious and 63.78% are internal transfers between wallets in the same linked cluster. The value that demonstrably reaches a named independent service is $187,861.35; the most generous bound, counting everything not provably manufactured, is $20.2 million. Payer, recipient, and value Gini coefficients all sit above 0.98, and the manufactured component resolves into a coherent operator-driven economy that is star-shaped, machine-timed, and gas-subsidized. The authors' framing is the load-bearing part: a settlement count measures how cheaply transactions can be manufactured, not how many agents are buying anything. Crypto analytics has run this play before. When wash trading hollowed out NFT marketplace volume, the raw number did not survive contact with the audits either, and venues and analytics providers shipped filtered volume metrics that excluded self-dealing until the filtered figure became the one people quoted. The same forcing function applies here, and applies harder: agentic commerce is being underwritten by investors and partners on exactly this throughput number, and a three-order-of-magnitude gap between the headline and the defensible floor turns an unfiltered count into a liability for whoever publishes it. The prediction: at least one x402 facilitator, official protocol dashboard, or major on-chain analytics provider begins publishing an x402 adoption metric that explicitly excludes manufactured or intra-cluster settlements — a filtered or net count, offered alongside or in place of the raw settlement total, with a documented exclusion methodology. Landing condition: by Q2 2027, one such filtered metric is published with its methodology visible, whether by the protocol's own stewards or by a third party the ecosystem cites.

reasoning.because: A 280-day x402 audit finds 21.20% of 136.7M settlements fictitious, 63.78% intra-cluster
reasoning.given: Wash-trade audits forced NFT venues onto filtered volume once the raw count lost credibility
reasoning.so_that: An x402 facilitator or chain-analytics provider publishes a settlement count that excludes manufactured volume
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; ≥1 x402 facilitator or chain-analytics provider ships the filter
reasoning.plain_language: Most payments between AI shopping agents turned out to be fake or self-dealing. Soon someone will publish a cleaned-up count that strips them out.

summary: A 280-day audit of the x402 agent-payment protocol finds 21.20% of its 136.7 million settlements fictitious and 63.78% internal to linked wallet clusters, with concentration Gini above 0.98. As wash-trading audits once did to NFT volume, expect a filtered x402 adoption metric by Q2 2027.
